C1.dialogue: A: How has hybrid teaching affected results? B: Slightly positive, though the gap between strong and weak pupils has widened.
C1.question: What has widened?
acceptable_answers: the gap between strong and weak pupils
the gap between the strong and weak pupils

C1.dialogue: A: Did management accept the consultants' advice? B: Mostly, but the plan to close the regional branch was shelved.
C1.question: What was shelved?
acceptable_answers: the plan to close the regional branch
the plan to close the branch

C1.dialogue: A: How would you sum up the residents' consultation? B: Lively, if somewhat dominated by concerns over increased traffic.
C1.question: What dominated the consultation?

C1.dialogue: A: Was the renovation of the station worth the disruption? B: On balance, yes, step-free access has made an enormous difference.
C1.question: What has made an enormous difference?

C1.dialogue: A: Why did the research team abandon the original method? B: It proved too costly to scale beyond a handful of sites.
C1.question: Why was the method abandoned?
acceptable_answers: it was too costly to scale
it was too expensive to scale up
it proved too costly to scale

C1.dialogue: A: How are you finding the transition to freelance work? B: Liberating, though the irregular income takes some getting used to.
C1.question: What takes some getting used to?

C1.dialogue: A: Did the orchestra's experiment with informal concerts pay off? B: Ticket sales among younger audiences have more than doubled.
C1.question: Among whom have ticket sales more than doubled?

C1.dialogue: A: What did the inspectors make of the care home? B: They praised the staff's warmth but criticised the outdated record keeping.
C1.question: What did the inspectors criticise?

C1.dialogue: A: Why are you reluctant to sign the lease? B: The break clause would effectively lock us in for five years.
C1.question: How long would the clause lock them in?

C1.dialogue: A: Has the brand's sustainability pledge been credible? B: Partially, their packaging has improved, but shipping emissions remain largely unaddressed.
C1.question: What remains largely unaddressed?

C1.dialogue: A: How did the judges evaluate the architecture entries? B: Primarily on how well each design integrated with its natural surroundings.
C1.question: What were the entries judged on primarily?
acceptable_answers: how well each design integrated with its natural surroundings
how well they fit their surroundings

C1.dialogue: A: Is the language exchange programme worth joining? B: If you're prepared to commit, conversational fluency improves remarkably quickly.
C1.question: What improves quickly?

C1.dialogue: A: Did the trial of driverless buses go smoothly? B: Technically, yes, but passengers were uneasy without a driver on board.
C1.question: Why were passengers uneasy?
acceptable_answers: there was no driver on board

C1.dialogue: A: Why is the bakery chain closing so many outlets? B: Rising energy costs have made its larger ovens prohibitively expensive to run.
C1.question: What has become too expensive to run?

C1.dialogue: A: How did the debate society fare at the national finals? B: They reached the semi-finals, which exceeded everyone's expectations.
C1.question: How far did they get?

C1.dialogue: A: Has the hospital's volunteer driver scheme been a success? B: Immensely, missed appointments among elderly patients have fallen sharply.
C1.question: Among whom have missed appointments fallen?

C1.dialogue: A: Why did the architect revise the plans? B: The original design would have overshadowed the neighbouring gardens.
C1.question: What would the original design have overshadowed?

C1.dialogue: A: What's your take on the new performance review process? B: It's more transparent, but the quarterly reviews feel somewhat excessive.
C1.question: What feels excessive?

C1.dialogue: A: Did the museum's late openings attract a new crowd? B: Very much so, mostly young professionals dropping in after work.
C1.question: Who mainly came to the late openings?

C1.dialogue: A: How did the conference organisers handle the speaker cancellation? B: They reshuffled the programme seamlessly, and most delegates barely noticed.
C1.question: Did most delegates notice?

C1.dialogue: A: Is the city's bike-sharing scheme financially viable? B: Not yet, it still relies heavily on advertising revenue.
C1.question: What does it rely on?

C1.dialogue: A: Why have so many families left the village? B: Mainly the lack of affordable housing for young people.
C1.question: What is the main reason?
acceptable_answers: a lack of affordable housing for young people

C1.dialogue: A: Was your thesis supervisor supportive? B: Exceptionally, she read every draft within days and offered incisive feedback.
C1.question: How quickly did she read drafts?

C1.dialogue: A: How did the chef react to the critic's scathing review? B: Graciously, he even invited her back to try the revised menu.
C1.question: What did the chef invite the critic to do?
acceptable_answers: come back and try the revised menu
come back to try the new menu

C1.dialogue: A: Has the online grocery service lived up to its promise? B: Deliveries are punctual, but substitutions are frequent and often bizarre.
C1.question: What is frequent and often bizarre?

C1.dialogue: A: Was the job interview as gruelling as you feared? B: Worse, there were three rounds, including a presentation to the directors.
C1.question: How many rounds were there?

C1.dialogue: A: Why did the charity rethink its fundraising strategy? B: Donations through street collections had plummeted, while online giving surged.
C1.question: What had plummeted?

C1.dialogue: A: How did the film festival handle the heatwave? B: Screenings were moved to the evening, and free water was provided throughout.
C1.question: When were screenings moved to?

C1.dialogue: A: Would you say the training course was value for money? B: Hardly, most of the content was freely available online.
C1.question: Why wasn't it value for money?
acceptable_answers: most of the content was freely available online
it was available online for free
the content was freely available online

C1.dialogue: A: How did the town respond to losing its only cinema? B: Residents crowdfunded a community screen in the old library.
C1.question: Where is the community screen?

C1.dialogue: A: Why did you turn down the board position? B: The time commitment was incompatible with my teaching schedule.
C1.question: What was the time commitment incompatible with?

C1.dialogue: A: How has the street market changed since the redevelopment? B: It's tidier, but many of the original traders have been priced out.
C1.question: What has happened to many original traders?

C1.dialogue: A: Was the hiking guide's advice useful? B: Invaluable, she steered us away from a route that had been washed out.
C1.question: What had happened to the route?

C1.dialogue: A: Has the company's mentoring programme been effective? B: Retention among junior staff has improved markedly since it was introduced.
C1.question: What has improved?

C1.dialogue: A: How did the audience respond to the experimental opera? B: Polarised, half gave a standing ovation while others sat in stunned silence.
C1.question: What did half the audience give?

C1.dialogue: A: Why is the vet piloting video consultations? B: To spare nervous animals the stress of travelling.
C1.question: Who is spared the stress of travelling?

C1.dialogue: A: Did the negotiations with the landlord prove fruitful? B: We secured a rent freeze, albeit in exchange for a longer tenancy.
C1.question: What did they agree to in exchange?

C1.dialogue: A: Has the bilingual signage been well received by visitors? B: Overwhelmingly, tourists say it makes navigating the old town far less daunting.
C1.question: What does it make less daunting?
acceptable_answers: finding their way around the old town

C1.dialogue: A: Why did your sister leave the law firm? B: The relentless hours left her no time for her family.
C1.question: What left her no time for her family?

C2.dialogue: A: How would you characterise the new director's leadership style? B: Consultative to a fault, decisions are deferred until consensus is all but guaranteed.
C2.question: When are decisions made?
acceptable_answers: when consensus is all but guaranteed

C2.dialogue: A: Did the biography shed new light on the composer's early life? B: Considerably, previously unpublished letters revealed an unexpectedly turbulent adolescence.
C2.question: What revealed a turbulent adolescence?

C2.dialogue: A: Was the conference's emphasis on sustainability merely rhetorical? B: Largely, the catering alone generated a staggering quantity of single-use plastic.
C2.question: What generated the plastic?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the seasoned editor respond to the author's resistance? B: Patiently, conceding minor points while holding firm on the structural cuts.
C2.question: What did the editor hold firm on?

C2.dialogue: A: Has the orchard's switch to organic methods been vindicated? B: Commercially, not yet, though the soil quality has improved beyond recognition.
C2.question: What has improved beyond recognition?

C2.dialogue: A: Is the professor's critique of the theory persuasive? B: Compelling in its rigour, though it rather conveniently sidesteps the most damaging counter-evidence.
C2.question: What does the critique sidestep?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the gallery justify deaccessioning the sculpture? B: It argued the proceeds would fund the conservation of far more significant works.
C2.question: What would the proceeds fund?
acceptable_answers: the conservation of far more significant works
the conservation of more significant works

C2.dialogue: A: Did the inquiry into the stadium's design flaws apportion blame? B: Studiously not, it attributed the failings to systemic rather than individual shortcomings.
C2.question: To what did it attribute the failings?

C2.dialogue: A: Was the author's memoir as candid as its publicity implied? B: Selectively so, it dwells on early hardships but glosses over later controversies.
C2.question: What does the memoir gloss over?

C2.dialogue: A: How has the craft brewery sustained its growth? B: By resisting the temptation to expand too rapidly, prioritising quality over volume.
C2.question: What does the brewery prioritise over volume?

C2.dialogue: A: Did the painter's late work mark a radical departure? B: Less a departure than a distillation, every superfluous detail was pared away.
C2.question: What was pared away?

C2.dialogue: A: Is the latest labour market report cause for optimism? B: Guardedly, employment is rising, but wages continue to lag behind inflation.
C2.question: What continues to lag behind inflation?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the curator reconcile the rival interpretations? B: She didn't, the exhibit presents both and lets visitors adjudicate.
C2.question: Who decides between the interpretations?

C2.dialogue: A: Was the tech firm's valuation justified by its fundamentals? B: Scarcely, it was buoyed almost entirely by investor enthusiasm for the sector.
C2.question: What buoyed the valuation?

C2.dialogue: A: Did the larger venue dilute the festival's intimacy? B: Somewhat, though clever staging preserved much of the original atmosphere.
C2.question: What preserved the atmosphere?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the scientist respond to claims that her data were flawed? B: She invited independent replication, which ultimately corroborated her findings.
C2.question: What corroborated her findings?

C2.dialogue: A: Has the heritage railway managed to remain solvent? B: Precariously, it depends on an ageing and dwindling pool of volunteers.
C2.question: What does the railway depend on?
acceptable_answers: an ageing and dwindling pool of volunteers

C2.dialogue: A: Was the negotiator's concession a sign of weakness? B: Quite the opposite, it was a calculated gambit to extract more later.
C2.question: What was the concession really?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the novelist handle the shifting timelines? B: Deftly, each chapter's opening line subtly anchors the reader in time.
C2.question: What anchors the reader in time?
acceptable_answers: the opening line of each chapter
the first line of each chapter

C2.dialogue: A: Did the restoration of the fresco attract criticism? B: Some purists objected that the colours had been rendered implausibly vivid.
C2.question: What did purists object to?

C2.dialogue: A: Is the historian's revisionist account gaining acceptance? B: Gradually, though older scholars remain wedded to the orthodox interpretation.
C2.question: Who remains wedded to the orthodox interpretation?

C2.dialogue: A: How has the island adapted to dwindling fish stocks? B: Many fishermen have pivoted to ecotourism, guiding visitors instead.
C2.question: What have many pivoted to?

C2.dialogue: A: Was the play true to the original novel? B: Irreverently unfaithful, yet it captured the novel's essence remarkably vividly.
C2.question: What did the adaptation capture?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the board justify the chief executive's generous severance? B: As a necessary inducement for a swift and uncontested departure.
C2.question: What was the severance meant to secure?

C2.dialogue: A: Has the remote research station proved worth its considerable cost? B: Unquestionably, its ice core data has transformed our understanding of past climates.
C2.question: What has the data transformed?

C2.dialogue: A: Is the minimalist aesthetic of the new library universally admired? B: Hardly, critics deride it as austere, while users praise its calm.
C2.question: What do users praise?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the athlete account for her unexpected loss of form? B: Candidly, she attributed it to burnout from an unrelenting competition schedule.
C2.question: What did she attribute it to?
acceptable_answers: burnout from an unrelenting competition schedule

C2.dialogue: A: Was the decision to pedestrianise the high street universally welcomed? B: Delivery firms grumbled, but residents relish the newfound tranquillity.
C2.question: What do residents relish?

C2.dialogue: A: Did the conductor's unorthodox tempi divide opinion? B: Sharply, purists were aghast, whereas newcomers found the performance exhilarating.
C2.question: How did newcomers find the performance?

C2.dialogue: A: How plausible is the claim that the manuscript is authentic? B: Increasingly so, the ink composition matches documents from the same period precisely.
C2.question: What matches documents from the same period?

C2.dialogue: A: Has the resort's environmental certification convinced sceptics? B: Few, given that its private jet transfers remain a prominently advertised perk.
C2.question: What remains a prominently advertised perk?

C2.dialogue: A: Did the mathematician's proof withstand scrutiny? B: Largely, though a subtle gap in the third section required a lengthy addendum.
C2.question: Where was the gap?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the filmmaker win over the reclusive community? B: Patiently, she spent almost two years earning their trust first.
C2.question: How long did she spend earning their trust?

C2.dialogue: A: Has the bakery's sourdough lost its distinction since expanding? B: Imperceptibly to most, though connoisseurs detect a slightly blander crumb.
C2.question: Who detects a difference?

C2.dialogue: A: What do you make of the critics' lukewarm reception of the album? B: Unsurprising, its subtleties reveal themselves only after repeated listening.
C2.question: When do its subtleties reveal themselves?

C2.dialogue: A: How did the expedition team cope when supplies ran low? B: Resourcefully, they foraged and rationed meticulously until the relief flight arrived.
C2.question: What arrived?

C2.dialogue: A: Was the philanthropist's donation as altruistic as it appeared? B: Not entirely, it conveniently secured naming rights to the new concert hall.
C2.question: What did the donation secure?
acceptable_answers: naming rights to the new concert hall
naming rights to the concert hall

C2.dialogue: A: Did the linguist's fieldwork yield anything unexpected? B: Remarkably, she documented a counting system with no word for any number above five.
C2.question: Above which number did the system have no words?

C2.dialogue: A: How has the veteran teacher stayed so effective? B: By remaining relentlessly curious and treating every cohort as entirely new.
C2.question: How does the teacher treat every cohort?

C2.dialogue: A: Has the ballet company's new artistic director revitalised it? B: Undeniably, the repertoire is bolder, though some longtime patrons have defected.
C2.question: Who has defected?

C2.dialogue: A: How credible was the travel writer's account of the journey? B: Embellished, certainly, but the essential itinerary has been independently verified.
C2.question: What has been independently verified?

C2.dialogue: A: Why did the observatory curtail its public programme? B: Light pollution from the expanding town had rendered most evening viewings futile.
C2.question: What rendered the viewings futile?
acceptable_answers: light pollution from the expanding town

C2.dialogue: A: Did the chef's foray into fusion cuisine succeed? B: Patchily, some combinations were inspired, while others were merely incongruous.
C2.question: Did all the combinations work?
